changes: Name normalized from 'Padamāpati' to 'Padmāpati'. 'padamā-' is read as svarabhakti spelling of 'padmā-', and 'padamāpatinamidaṃ' as 'padmāpatinā idaṃ'. Confidence lowered to medium because the cataloguer marked the form (!).
Evidence shortened to the relevant substring.
Purpose reworded: the 'anena prīyatāṃ...' line is a dedicatory formula, not a statement of purpose.
Notes added on the era mismatch: VS 1830 normally corresponds to ŚS 1695, not 1696, so 1696 is probably the current (vartamāna) year. Notes also cover the name reading and the lacuna.

purpose: dedicatory formula: anena prīyatāṃ devo bhagavān pārvatīpatiḥ
notes: Date: Phālguna of VS 1830 (Caitrādi) falls in February/March 1774 CE. The usual equivalent would be ŚS 1695 (expired), so the stated ŚS 1696 is probably the current (vartamāna) Śaka year. This is a one-year mismatch between the two eras, not a real conflict; both point to about 1774 CE. Name: the corrupt 'padamāpatinamidaṃ' is read as 'padmāpatinā idaṃ (pustakam)', giving the instrumental of Padmāpati (the catalogue has Padamāpati). The verse naming Viśvanātha as kuladaivata has a lacuna; it refers to a deity, not a person. 'pusta°°' is truncated, presumably for pustakam.
